_about: Card seeds for the Factory to rebuild itself as the constitutional institutions. There are no named roles: from the first card, the Factory's agents work as a collective. Any agent pulls the oldest ready card it can do; a model of another family checks it; the rules in the Ledger do the managing. Dog-food build: no lab, no shadow periods, no trial. Every card is grounded in the code by whoever pulls it: it cites the files and commit it read. A seed whose premise does not hold is marked down to its author with evidence (R8) and goes back to Planning, never quietly reshaped. A puller may split a seed into child cards that together meet the seed's acceptance contract; seeds are never merged, dropped or widened without Isa. [PROPOSED] values are for Isa to ratify in AR-13; [PLACEHOLDER] values are resolved only by the open item named.

phases.name: Protect, measure and operate
phases.intent: Start pulling as a collective, protect governance, add trustworthy memory, measure live from day one, and operate live inside the Factory.
entry: AR-14 loads the Phase 0 cards into the pull queue
exit: Isa approves the phase exit through the interim gate (C0.02)

phases.name: Rules, Market, Review and Scaler
phases.intent: Layer the pull rules, licences, Market, Review and elastic capacity onto the collective's pull. Each part is switched on as soon as it passes its acceptance contract.
entry: AR-19 signed before C1.20, C1.21 and C1.22 start; AR-09b before C1.22
AR-20 signed before C1.23, C1.24 and C1.25 start
exit: Isa approves the phase exit through the interim gate (C0.02)

phases.name: Audit, Release Gate and live operation
phases.intent: Mark the markers, gate every change including governance, and give live operation an owner.
exit: Protected governance paths now pass the Release Gate and Isa (C2.02 replaces the interim gate)

phases.name: Inquiry, Council and Planning
phases.intent: Stand up the three deliberative institutions. Low volume lets them start semi-manually under their charters.
exit: Release Gate promotion of the phase

phases.name: Operate, monitor and improve
phases.intent: No trial and no end date. The Factory runs on its new lines, compares itself weekly with the model, judges X1-X14 as data accrues, and amends through the Release Gate and Isa.

cards.title: Register this pack as a versioned, hash-verified record
cards.intent: The pack is the constitution's first ratified input. Store it so every later card can cite the exact version it was built from.
scope: Store factory-pack.json and manifest.json; verify every sha256 in the manifest
Record the ratification (AR-13) as a human-authored record
Record the mapping from pack card IDs to the Factory's card IDs, including child cards from splits
acceptance: pack/test_pack.py passes on the stored copy
A changed byte in any stored pack file is detected by hash check
Every Factory card created from the pack carries its pack card ID and the pack version

cards.title: Protected governance paths, with an interim gate
cards.intent: No change approves itself. Before the Factory edits its own rules, the files that hold the constitution, charters, Ledger rules, Scaler and burn-cap settings, and this pack are protected.
scope: Confirm the protected path list in AR-11 against the code: the files holding the constitution, charters, Ledger rules, Scaler and burn-cap settings, and this pack
Block any merge touching a protected path unless it carries an approval record from Isa and a pass from an agent of another model family than the change's author
This interim gate holds until the Release Gate exists (C2.02)
Alert on any attempted change to a protected path
acceptance: A test change to a protected path without an approval record is blocked
The same change with an approval record and an independent pass merges
The author of a change cannot supply its own approval
The protected path list is itself protected
evidence: Blocked and allowed test merges recorded

cards.title: Append-only Ledger beside today's operational state
cards.intent: Memory is governed, and facts and claims are kept apart. Add an append-only, replayable Ledger alongside the existing SQLite state without disturbing running work.
scope: Append-only event log with a hash chain
Facts (tool output, git state, usage, timings), claims (model assertions) and derived values (rule outputs) in separate tables
Operational state rebuildable from the Ledger (projections)
SQL as canonical operational state; Git as the artifact authority (DQ9)
The parked schema docs/design-parked/ledger-schema.sql is a reference: its assignment, draw and shadow-price tables are superseded by pull (R1) and must not be built
acceptance: UPDATE and DELETE on Ledger tables abort
Rebuilding projections from the Ledger reproduces the live projection exactly
The Factory keeps working while the Ledger is written alongside its existing state
Any recorded rule decision can be recomputed from the Ledger (replay)
evidence: Tests for append-only enforcement and replay

cards.title: Adapters record usage for every model invocation
cards.intent: Token use, cost and throttling are the inputs to the Scaler, the burn cap and calibration. Record them as facts from the adapter, never as model claims.
scope: Per invocation: provider, model ID and version, reasoning effort, time to first token, generation time, tool and wait time, input, cached-input and output tokens, list-price cost, throttle or error codes
Keyed to idea, card, value-stream step and attempt
acceptance: Every model invocation in a sample week has a usage record
Metered cost reconciles with the actual costs the Owner enters from vendor invoices, subscriptions and cloud credits (C0.09) within [PROPOSED] 2%
Throttle events (for example HTTP 429) are recorded with the rate-limit headers the vendor returns

cards.title: Key custody: no secret in the Ledger, a fingerprint for attribution
cards.intent: The Owner holds the vendor accounts and keys; they are hashed in the Factory. The Ledger may record which key was used, never the key.
scope: Adapters obtain credentials from where the Owner keeps them today; the puller finds this in the code and records it (OI-04)
The Ledger records a key fingerprint (hash) per vendor account and invocation
Secret scanning of the Ledger, logs, prompts and the pack
acceptance: A secret scan of the Ledger, logs and repository finds no key material
Rotating a key changes its fingerprint and does not break usage attribution
A model invocation cannot be made with a key the Owner has not registered

cards.title: Record every value-stream step for today's Factory
cards.intent: Measure today's Factory on the same steps the simulation uses, so the two can be compared.
scope: Map the Factory's current workflow stages onto the value-stream steps: discover, challenge, human intent ratification, design, plan, plan check, human plan ratification, build, review, security review, merge and CI, audit, acceptance test, release, deploy, live operation (docs/idea/value-stream.md §2)
Per card and idea: start, end, waiting time and outcome at each step; rework and its cause
Steps today's Factory does not perform are recorded as absent, not inferred
Every step routed to Isa is a timed stage: request, decision and send-back rounds are recorded like any institution's work (M22)
acceptance: The stage-to-step mapping is written down and ratified by Isa
For a sample week, every idea and card has a complete step timeline or an explicit 'absent step' record
Lead time, change-failure rate and step hours can be computed by SQL query alone

cards.title: Record dependencies and the artifact versions each card read
cards.intent: R17 needs to know what each card depends on and which version of its prerequisites it built against. X13 needs the Factory's real coupling.
scope: Dependencies between requirements and between cards, as planned
The artifact versions (commits) each card read when built
Stale rebuilds: cards redone because a prerequisite changed
acceptance: For a sample week, coupling (share of dependent requirement pairs) and stale rebuilds per idea can be computed by SQL query
Every card's read versions are recorded at build time

cards.title: Record defect provenance and which families missed it
cards.intent: Blind spots shared by every model family are the one failure no organisation fixes. Measure them, and every check's catch rate.
scope: For every defect found anywhere, including live: where it was introduced, which check caught it, which checks passed it, and the model family behind each check
Deterministic evidence (tests, CI, typed contracts) recorded as first-class evidence (DQ10)
acceptance: For a sample week, the catch rate of each check and the share of escaped defects missed by every family that checked them are computable by SQL query

cards.title: Idea value ledger: baseline at intake, actuals as they happen
cards.intent: An idea is worth nothing without action. Each idea carries a baseline from the pack's analysis at intake, and the baseline is replaced by actual output and actual cost as they happen.
scope: At intake: a baseline cost to artifact from the pack's cost model (claim CL-02 per clean idea, the menu's token prices) and the expected return the idea's Alignment Record states, in USD

Segment 1, idea to first artifact (merged code or ratified document): metered model spend (C0.04), plus the actual costs the Owner enters (vendor invoices, subscriptions, cloud credits such as development sessions), plus recorded human hours
Segment 2: ratification, production and return events, with the actual value the Owner records in USD
Ideas with no action are recorded as 'no action', value zero
The cost model is re-based from actuals every week; baselines for new ideas use the re-based model
acceptance: Every idea has a baseline at intake and, once acted on, an actual segment 1 cost computable from Ledger facts and Owner entries
The Owner can enter an actual cost against a vendor, a period or an idea
A weekly report shows baseline against actual per idea, and the model's re-based cost per clean idea
evidence: Value report for a sample period

cards.title: Package the simulation twin and reproduce the recorded results
cards.intent: The value-stream simulation is the Factory's model of itself. Make it runnable inside the Factory on CPU (no model spend), pinned to the pack's commit, with its parameters read from a file.
scope: probes/value-stream/vs_sim.py and the modules it imports (probes/institutions/factory_sim.py, probes/portfolio6/select6.py), pinned by the hashes in manifest.json
Every assumed parameter listed in the pack's twin_parameters read from one parameter file
Output the same measures as live (M01-M05, M11-M13)
acceptance: python3 -m unittest discover -s probes/value-stream passes inside the Factory
With the default parameter file, the institutions with the six reproduce 24.9 clean ideas a week (claim CL-01)
Changing a parameter in the file changes the run; no parameter is hard-coded outside it

cards.title: Live measurement from day one
cards.intent: There is no study period. The measures accrue as the Factory works, and every figure is live from the first card.
scope: C0.04-C0.09 switched on for all work from the start
Weekly: the demand profile, token use per card and step, pass rates per model, step and tier, coupling, catch rates, change-failure rate, lead times, cost per idea to artifact, human attention hours
acceptance: Every measure M01-M18 has a live value each week, or a recorded reason it cannot be measured yet
Variance per measure is reported, so AR-08's baseline standards can be adjusted

cards.title: Recalibrate the model weekly from live data
cards.intent: The model's assumptions are the baseline. Replace each with live data as soon as there is enough of it, automatically and without model spend.
scope: Weekly, for each twin parameter: fitted value from live data, or 'not enough data yet' with the assumption kept
Sensitivity: which unmeasured parameters move the model's figures most
The weekly model run and its figures for the coming week (M01, M03, M04, M05, M12)
acceptance: Every parameter in twin_parameters is marked fitted (with the measure and period used) or assumed (with the reason)
Each week's parameter file and figures are stored as a versioned record before the week's live data arrives

cards.title: Weekly report and alarms: live against the model
cards.intent: One weekly view that compares the Factory with its own predictions, built on SQL views, no new tool.
scope: SQL views for every measure M01-M20
Weekly comparison with that week's model figures (C0.12)
Alarm when live results fall outside the model by more than 25% (X9) or an experiment's falsification criterion is met: the alarm opens a card, it does not stop work
Isa's attention hours and spend against the ceiling every week
X1: pull against the old role routing, using the Factory's records from before the pack as the baseline
acceptance: The report is generated from Ledger queries alone
Each figure links to the query that produced it
An alarm creates a card with the evidence attached

cards.title: Live operation inside the Factory: detect, restore, hotfix
cards.intent: Live operation is part of the Factory. From the first change, the Factory detects its own incidents, restores service and fixes forward by its own rules.
scope: Detect: the Ledger raises an incident on failed runs, error-rate or throughput control limits, or a failed smoke test after a change
Restore: the owner reverts the change that caused it (Git) and records restore time
Hotfix: a card that is pulled, built, reviewed and released like any other
Attribute: change-failure rate and restore time are marked against the releasing change and its producers (R8, R12)
Until the Release Gate exists, incidents and restores are top-priority cards in the pull queue: any agent pulls them, and one of another family checks the restore
acceptance: A deliberately failed change is detected, reverted and recorded with restore time
A hotfix card goes through the normal flow, not a side door
Every incident names the change that caused it

cards.title: The pull queue: the collective pulls from day one
cards.intent: No one assigns work, from the first card. Encode in the Factory what the collective already does under the pack's integrity contract: any agent pulls the oldest ready card it can do, and an agent of another family checks it.
scope: One queue of ready cards; an agent with a free slot pulls the oldest in the highest tier it is licensed for (R1, R3)
Starting licences from today's mapping of models to work (R11): whatever a model did well under the old routing is its starting licence
The check on every card is done by a model of another family (R18), after the deterministic checks (tests, CI)
The old role routing stops assigning work; its history stays in the records
A puller may split a card into child cards, recorded against the parent
acceptance: No card in the Factory is assigned to a named role or a named model
Every accepted card has a check by another model family, or a recorded waiver (R13)
A pull is reproducible from the queue state and the licences
evidence: Queue and licence records for the first week of pulls

cards.title: The harness kernel: one for every institution
cards.intent: Agent = model + harness. Build the shared kernel every institution's harness runs on, so each institution is a tailored harness and models are interchangeable workers inside it.
scope: Primitive tools only: sandboxed worktree file access, sandboxed shell and CLI, retrieval from the Ledger, lifecycle hooks; each institution's charter grants a subset

Context assembly fresh per pull from the Ledger (R24), in a fixed cache-first order: constitution and charter, rules and the agent's own record, repository snapshot, then the card and its evidence; long histories enter as Ledger summaries linked to sources
Feed-forward guards (licence and floor, independence, output schemas, protected paths, readiness) and feedback sensors (tests, linters, CI, typed contracts) as middleware, before any model judgment
Structured traces of every call, tool use, latency and outcome to the Ledger, classifiable by cause (R8)
Trajectory budgets on tokens, time and retries per card; loops without progress stop and escalate or hand back
Harness components (tools, context policies, guards, prompts) as versioned files
Domain-neutral: the kernel holds no software-specific step, check or defect definition; those come from the domain pack (software first)
acceptance: No agent keeps state between pulls: a pull's context is reproducible from the Ledger and the charter version
The context for a card is assembled in the fixed order, and the prompt-cache hit rate is recorded per call (M25)
A tool outside the institution's charter cannot be called
A trajectory over budget stops and leaves a trace with its cause
evidence: Kernel tests; replay of context assembly

cards.title: Self-hosted model gateway: any model, any route, by configuration
cards.intent: Model flexibility is core, so it lives in the Factory's own layer, not a rented one. A self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM or equivalent) is the one model interface: any model swaps for another by configuration, the Owner keeps the keys, and no third party sits in the data path unless a route is chosen for it.
scope: Run a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, open source, or equivalent) inside the Factory as the single model interface for every harness
Model, reasoning effort and route are configuration: a direct vendor API, or an aggregator route (OpenRouter first; Vercel AI Gateway as a trial route)
Keys stay in the Owner's custody, hashed in the Factory; the gateway reads them from the Owner's store and the Ledger records fingerprints only (C0.05)
Per route: prompt caching passed through with sticky sessions; data collection denied and zero retention requested where the route offers it (R15)
No model-specific logic in any harness; a lint check fails the build on a named model outside configuration
A swap takes effect at the next pull; the new model starts under R5's fast track
The gateway is a live service: its failures are incidents handled by C0.16, and its configuration is a protected path
acceptance: Swapping one menu model for another is a configuration change with no code change, shown by a test
The same card runs through a direct route and through an aggregator route, with usage, latency and cache hits recorded for both (M08, M25)
No key material leaves the Owner's store: a secret scan of the gateway, Ledger and logs finds none
A named model in harness code fails the lint check
Stopping the gateway raises an incident and a restore within C0.16's flow

cards.title: Card schema: tier, requirements, dependencies, interfaces, contract
cards.intent: Cards must carry what the rules read.
scope: Absolute work tier (1-3, H5)
Requirement links; dependencies; the interfaces between requirements named in the plan (DQ11)
Acceptance contract hash, including locked tests
Value-stream step; author and the author's model family
One requirement per build invocation until X12 measures otherwise
acceptance: A card without a tier, requirement link or contract is rejected at creation
Card versions are immutable; a change creates a new version

cards.title: Tier-setting rules in Planning
cards.intent: Card difficulty is set by rules over card facts, never by a model's judgement, and corrected by escalation.
scope: Tier from card facts: size, files, risk paths, dependencies (Idea Record §2)
Which card facts set the tier, per institution (DQ1)
acceptance: The same card facts always give the same tier (replay)
The rule set is a protected path

cards.title: API access for the seven-model menu, under the data rule
cards.intent: Staff the menu on API tokens, with no tier that trains on our data, and read real rate limits.
scope: Configure the menu in the pack's menu section through the self-hosted gateway (C0.19), on the routes AR-10 approves: direct vendor routes for the two anchors (Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-5.6 Terra); OpenRouter as the aggregator route where its catalogue or provider fallback is needed (Muse Spark 1.3; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and Ling 3.0 Flash across hosts); Vercel AI Gateway trialled as a second aggregator route [PROPOSED]
A route is registered only with a recorded no-training confirmation for that tier (R15); Muse Spark's Contributor tier is excluded
Vendor rate limits recorded as Scaler caps (replacing the assumed 8 per model, 48 in all)
A second route per model where AR-10 names one; the Ledger chooses routes on measured quality, cost and speed (X19)
acceptance: Registering a route without a no-training confirmation fails
Each menu model answers a test invocation and its usage is recorded (C0.04)
Each route's rate limit is stored as a fact with its source

cards.title: Licences and pull: hardest first, oldest first
cards.intent: Extend C0.17's pull with the full licence ladder and the agent's view of its own record.
scope: R1 pull; R2 licence ladder; R3 hardest first, oldest first, no choice within a tier
R10: at pull time the agent sees its licences, recent rate against the standard and its recent markdown reasons; it may decline without a markdown; repeated declines return the licence
R11 start state: C0.17's starting licences; menu models not in today's mapping start from their Artificial Analysis band as prior (§5.1) and move on live evidence (OI-12)
The Ledger views each agent sees at pull time (DQ5)

Harness (Market, working): sandboxed worktree, shell, tests and its own branch, no merge; context is the card, contract, reviewed prerequisites and its own record; readiness check on arrival; hands unfit cards back to Planning
acceptance: An agent cannot pull a card above its licence
Within a tier, the pulled card is always the oldest
An agent's pull view contains only its own record
Every pull is replayable from the Ledger

cards.title: The ladder: promotion, two-speed demotion, fast track
cards.intent: Success and velocity push an agent up to the hardest tier it can sustain; failure moves it down.
scope: R5 as written, with the constants set once in the constitution (pack: constitution.constants)
Quality standards per institution and tier from AR-08: baseline from the analysis, adjusted from live variance
A minimum sample per tier before velocity comparisons count (RK4)
acceptance: Promotion credit +1 per accepted card at home tier, -4 per markdown; stretch cards compulsory at the credit threshold
Promotion after 20 trial cards meeting the tier's quality standard
Gross demotion (over 2x the standard) after 10 cards; marginal (over 1.25x) only after two consecutive failing batches of 20
A failed promotion doubles the credit needed next time, capped at 2x; a new model needs 5 credit until its first failed promotion
Every licence change cites the rule and the counts that caused it
evidence: Rule tests against the pull-rules simulation's scenarios (probes/pull-rules)

cards.title: Hard-work reserve for capped agents (dormant under API tokens)
cards.intent: R7 protects a subscription cap for hard work. The menu runs on API tokens, so no seat is capped today; the rule must exist for any subscription seat P8 admits.
scope: R7 as written, applied only to agents with a subscription cap
Uncapped agents unaffected
acceptance: With no capped agent, the rule changes no decision (test)
With a simulated capped agent, it spends below its home tier only the capacity above what its home tier needs at 75% of full speed until reset

cards.title: Attribution with evidenced reason codes
cards.intent: Every markdown lands on the producer that caused it.
scope: R8 reason codes and the evidence each requires (DQ3)
Implementation to implementer; unclear or wrong card to its author in Planning; review miss found later to the reviewer and the implementer; infrastructure to nobody
acceptance: A markdown without a reason code and evidence is rejected
Card-caused markdowns are counted against the card's author, not the builder

cards.title: Markers are marked; late marks count double
cards.intent: Marking is accountable in both directions, and escaped defects cost more.
scope: R9: a pass later overturned by Audit, or a markdown overturned as unfounded, counts against the reviewer under R5
R12: an Audit finding weeks later applies like an immediate markdown, counted twice
acceptance: An overturned pass changes the reviewer's record
A late Audit finding is weighted twice in the producer's record

cards.title: No orphan tiers, with recorded waivers; escalation optional
cards.intent: Small teams deadlock without R13. Keep work moving and record every relaxation.
scope: R13: cards waiting at a tier with no licensed agent past a set time give the best agent one tier below stretch cards; if none, split in Planning or escalate to Isa
R13 may relax licences, independence and seat rules, each with a Ledger record (Idea Record §5.3)
R6 escalation is optional (§3.2): build it switchable, default per AR-13
acceptance: No card waits beyond the R13 limit without a waiver or escalation record
Every waiver names the rule relaxed, the card and the reason
evidence: Deadlock tests with one-model and two-model rosters

cards.title: Family independence
cards.intent: No model reviews, audits or releases work by a model of its own family.
scope: R18: family = vendor; instances and siblings are one epistemic source
If no other family is available, the waiver is recorded (R13)
acceptance: A same-family review, audit or release is refused unless a waiver record exists
Instances of one model count as one model

cards.title: High-impact licence floors
cards.intent: The steps where a mistake costs most need the most reliable models, chosen by evidence.
scope: R19: design, plan, plan red-team, security review, acceptance test and release need a pass chance of at least 0.8; other steps 0.6; review 0.5
Pass chance from the same evidence as every licence: the Artificial Analysis prior, then live records
acceptance: A model below a step's floor cannot take that step
When a model's record changes, its eligibility re-sorts without manual change

cards.title: Evidence-gated dependencies
cards.intent: Build only on reviewed work.
scope: R17: each card reviewed as built; no whole-idea barrier
A dependent card becomes available only when its prerequisite has passed review
A rework invalidates only the dependants whose inputs changed
The Ledger records the artifact versions each card read (C0.07)
acceptance: A dependent card is not pullable before its prerequisite passes review
After a rework, exactly the dependants that read the changed version are invalidated
No waiting limit converts to building on unreviewed work (the hybrid was tested and loses)

cards.title: The Scaler: elastic instances started and stopped by rule
cards.intent: Agents are instances of menu models, started and stopped by Ledger arithmetic, not by an agent.
scope: R14 as written (pack: parameters PR-01 to PR-09)

Price every queued task on every licensed model clearing the 0.8 floor: ($/busy hour x hours + time value x elapsed hours, latency included) / pass chance; cheapest price wins. Time value starts at $0.5 an hour (PR-21) and moves on live evidence
Target = busy instances + ceil(queued hours / drain target); held cards count as demand; clamp to vendor rate limits (C1.03)
Start the shortfall; stop instances idle 30 minutes beyond target
Cost-band pull at 1.5x unless the task has waited an hour
Instances of one model are one model for independence
Allocation has no model harness: the Scaler and licences are deterministic Ledger functions, replayable
acceptance: Every start and stop cites the counts and rule that caused it, and replays
No instance takes a task below the floor or outside the cost band before the wait expires
Rate limits read from C1.03 are never exceeded
evidence: Rule tests; replay; comparison with the twin's Scaler on the same queue

cards.title: Burn cap and monthly ceiling
cards.intent: Spend follows demand, within limits Isa sets.
scope: R16: running instances burn at most 2x the trailing seven-day average ($/hour)
Monthly ceiling = expected demand x cost per clean idea x 1.5; initial value from AR-05, reset from measured volume (C0.11)
When the cap binds, trim the most expensive model first
acceptance: Simulated overspend is trimmed before the cap is exceeded
The ceiling and cap are protected paths
Isa is notified when the monthly ceiling is [PROPOSED] 80% spent

cards.title: Rolling portfolio policy
cards.intent: The menu changes on evidence, never by chasing the leaderboard.
scope: P1 two top-tier models from two vendors, repaired at once
P2 no vendor above half the seats
P6 new models earn seats on evidence: one trial seat at a time; replaces the weakest incumbent only if its Ledger value per dollar beats it by 10%
P7 never chase the leaderboard
P8 match the help-down rule to how the seat is paid; top seats on API tokens
acceptance: A menu with fewer than two top-tier vendors triggers a repair record at once
A new model enters only through a trial seat with a recorded comparison

cards.title: Review
cards.intent: Is this work acceptable? Decided blind, deterministic checks first.
scope: Reviewers blind to author; open standing to challenge with evidence; other verdicts visible only after committing one's own
Deterministic checks first: build, tests, static analysis, CI, typed contracts (DQ10)
A reproduced defect beats any number of approvals

Harness (Review, reviewing): read-only diff; runs tests, linters, static analysis and reproductions; never sees author identity or reasoning; deterministic checks first; hands work without evidence back to the Market
acceptance: A review cannot see the author's identity or reasoning
A failing deterministic check blocks acceptance whatever the model reviews say
A reproduced defect overturns prior approvals

cards.title: Readiness hand-back at every boundary
cards.intent: A card that is not fit for purpose goes back before anyone builds on it. Every institution checks what it receives, as part of the pull.
scope: A readiness contract per institution: enough detail, the interfaces named, acceptance criteria the receiver can test
The puller checks the card against it before starting work; an unfit card is handed back at once to the producing institution with the reason (R21)
The producer is marked under R8; hand-backs and rounds per card are recorded at every boundary (M21)
Applies at every boundary: Planning to Market, Market to Review, Review to Release Gate, and to anything routed to Isa
acceptance: A card missing detail, interfaces or testable criteria is handed back before any build spend, with a reason code
Every hand-back is attributed to the producing institution
Hand-backs and rounds per card are reported weekly by boundary

cards.title: Edge cases as evidence: sealed scenario tests and challenge tests
cards.intent: Model-written review shares model blind spots. Edge cases become deterministic evidence: sealed tests from the contract's failure scenarios, and challenge tests written by another family before it reads the code.
scope: Failure scenarios in every acceptance contract: until Inquiry types them (C3.05), Planning or the card's author writes them; each becomes a locked test sealed from the builder, inside the contract hash (C1.01)
Challenge tester: at first review, a model of another family (R18) writes boundary, property-based and fuzz tests from the contract alone, and commits them before the code is visible to it
A failing sealed or challenge test is a reproduced defect (principle 3): it blocks acceptance whatever the model reviews say
Challenge testers are markers: a defect that escapes past their tests counts against them (R9)

Effort: about 30% of the card's hours [PROPOSED: the model's assumption]. Challenge tests start on every card; the Ledger keeps them by tier where they catch defects review passes and stops them where they do not (R26)
Harness (Review, reviewing): the challenge tester sees the contract and its failure scenarios only, until its tests are committed
acceptance: The build harness cannot read or edit sealed tests
A challenge tester's tests are committed before the code is visible to it (manifest audit)
A failing sealed or challenge test blocks acceptance
Each defect's provenance record (C0.08) shows whether a sealed or challenge test caught it, and the family that wrote the test
Challenge-test catches beyond review are reported weekly by tier, and the rule that keeps or stops them cites them

cards.title: Self-origination: Ledger signals become briefs
cards.intent: The Factory does not wait to be told. Its own record raises signals by rule, and each signal becomes a brief the collective works like any other. No ninth institution.
scope: Signals by rule, no model in the control path: escaped defects or incidents clustering on a component; all-family misses (X11); repeated hand-backs or stale rebuilds; a rising cost per clean idea; repeated agent work (R25); a weekly standing brief
Each signal becomes a brief with its evidence and a baseline value at intake (C0.09); a signal that matches an open brief is attached to it by rule
Until Inquiry runs (C3.05), the collective pulls originated briefs like any card, checked by another family; ratification follows the envelope (C1.22)
Budget: originated ideas use at most 20% of the monthly ceiling (R16, R27); beyond it, they wait
Marked by realised value (M07): ideas left with no action count against the contributions behind them
acceptance: Every originated brief cites the signal, the rule and the Ledger facts that raised it
Originated spend is reported weekly against its 20% share
Realised value per dollar is reported for originated ideas and for Isa's briefs side by side (X22)

cards.title: Ratification envelope and Isa's attention queue
cards.intent: Ratification is a problem to solve, not a ceiling to accept. Isa ratifies what only she can; rules ratify the rest inside bounds she sets, and her sample keeps them honest.
scope: The envelope Isa sets (AR-09b): baseline cost, reversible by canary rollback, no protected governance path, no new vendor, data flow or regulated claim, no disputed proposition
Inside: ratified by rule once the Alignment Record passes the envelope check; Isa reviews a random 10% afterwards (R28)
An overturn by Isa is a late mark (R12) on the producers and narrows the envelope at once; 20 rule ratifications without an overturn widen it one step, up to the ceiling Isa sets

Outside: Isa's queue, ordered by expected value per minute of her time (C0.09 baseline), in one digest. No fixed weekly budget, because her time varies (Isa, 1 Oct 2026): her turnaround is measured (M22), and she is alerted when an idea outside the envelope waits more than a week
Always Isa: amendments, standards, governance changes, R13 escalations
Envelope bounds and ceiling: [PLACEHOLDER: Isa sets them in AR-09b (OI-10)]
acceptance: Every ratification records who ratified it (Isa or the envelope rule) and the rule that routed it
Isa's sample is drawn at random; no producer can exclude an idea from it
Weekly report: Isa's hours (M17) and turnaround (M22), queue wait, share inside the envelope, sample overturn rate and envelope step (M28)

cards.title: Recorded behaviour as the oracle: record, select, replay
cards.intent: Model checks share model blind spots; past behaviour does not. Live use is recorded, the most covering recordings are kept, and every change is replayed old against new before it merges.
scope: Record real use in live operation (C0.16): sessions, requests with their responses, and the Ledger's own transitions
Each week, keep the few hundred recordings that cover the most behaviour with the least repetition (R29); coverage measured on the code paths they reach
At merge, replay against the old and the new version with recorded responses, so the replay is deterministic; from C2.02, the Release Gate replays again before any canary

A model of another family (R18) classifies each difference against the card's contract: unintended is a reproduced defect (principle 3); intended but not in the contract is handed back to Planning (R21)
Option A (Isa, 5 Oct 2026): the regression set is recorded live use, never a lab set

Prototype first (Isa, 5 Oct 2026): Isa is the only user, so recording runs on her own use with no consent process; redaction at capture, counsel review and anything regulated (Heliosvera included) wait for the pre-release gate (OI-21)
acceptance: Replays of the same recording on the same version give the same result
Every unintended difference blocks the merge with its recording attached
The replay set's coverage and age are reported weekly

cards.title: Lessons from corrections: scoped, approved, expiring
cards.intent: An approved correction changes what happens next. Lessons keep Isa's and each user's working judgment, and outlive every model swap.
scope: Proposed from Isa's send-backs and overturns (C1.22), recurring R8 reasons (C1.08) and, once EvryMynd joins, a user's corrections
Each lesson records its owner (the Factory or a user), scope (institution, domain, kind of work), source, author, approval status and review date, 90 days by default (R30)
Approved by the author of the correction, or by the Release Gate for a recurring review reason
The harness kernel (C0.18) puts approved lessons in scope into each pull's context, cited; agents show which lesson they applied
A user's lessons stay in that user's store and never enter the Factory's shared memory or any training (R15)
A correction that recurs after a lesson exists counts against the lesson; a lapsed lesson leaves context until approved again
acceptance: No lesson enters context outside its scope or after its review date
Every applied lesson is cited in the output that used it
Repeated corrections per scope are reported weekly, before and after each lesson (X26)

cards.title: Decision rights and outward actions
cards.intent: Nothing leaves the Factory without the right to send it. Every charter says who may recommend, approve, communicate and execute, and which actions are allowed, ask or never.
scope: A rights table per charter and per owner: recommend, approve, communicate, execute; each action allowed, ask or never (R31)
Outward communication or action (sending, publishing, contacting a vendor or customer) is ask by default, routed to Isa or to the user who owns the matter
Never without Isa or the owning user: spending money, signing, any regulated claim (Heliosvera's FDA and HIPAA exposure included)
The tool layer enforces the table: an outward tool call without the right is refused and logged
A rights entry changes only through the Release Gate and its owner; until C2.02 exists, through the interim gate (C0.02)
acceptance: An outward action without a recorded right is refused, and the refusal is logged
Every outward action that ran cites the right and approval behind it
Rights changes appear only through the gate, with their owner's approval

cards.title: Audit
cards.intent: Is assurance trustworthy? Auditors outside the work's provenance chain mark the markers.
scope: Random plus risk-weighted samples (the model used 10%)
Planted defects with known answers, which also test the auditors
Isa's sample
Findings feed R9 and R12 (C1.09)
Harness (Audit, auditing): read-only; planted-defect registry and Ledger sampling; sees contract and final artifact, never the review discussion
acceptance: No auditor audits work in its own provenance chain or family
Planted defects are recorded with their catch or miss

cards.title: Release Gate
cards.intent: Is an accepted change safe to run inside the Factory? Criteria fixed before data.
scope: Approvers from different families, blind, with one seated dissenter; cooling-off period; no version approves itself
Canary results against criteria fixed in advance
Acceptance test (QA) of the whole idea and release approval (value-stream steps 11-12)
Takes over protected governance paths from the interim gate (C0.02): rule changes pass the Release Gate and Isa
Harness (Release Gate, releasing): canary controls, rollback and metrics, no code edit; criteria fixed before data; hands unproven changes back to Review
acceptance: A change cannot be approved by a version of itself
Release criteria are recorded before canary data exists
A protected-path change now requires the Release Gate and Isa

cards.title: Release Gate takes over live operation
cards.intent: Live operation stays inside the Factory. The Release Gate, which let the change in, owns restoring from it.
scope: Move C0.16's incident, restore and hotfix flow from the pull queue's top priority to the Release Gate's charter
Hotfix cards pulled by the Market and reviewed by Review; restores decided by the Release Gate; the Ledger marks change-failure rate and restore time
acceptance: Every incident has the Release Gate as owner, a restore time and, where needed, a hotfix card
Change-failure rate and restore time are recorded as evidence against the releasing change

cards.title: Configurations as trial proposals
cards.intent: Step affinities found by search are trials, never the constitution.
scope: R20: the Ledger may propose step affinities from its own records as a trial configuration
Compared with the institutions on the same work; adopted only on evidence
Lapses automatically when the roster changes or a reserved pool is empty
acceptance: A configuration without a recorded comparison cannot be adopted
Removing a model from a reserved pool ends the configuration automatically

cards.title: Harness evolution: attributed traces, predicted edits
cards.intent: The harness, not the model, is the unit of self-improvement. Edits are attributed, predicted, trialled and adopted on evidence.
scope: Classify every failed or reworked card's trace by cause: model error, tool or tool documentation, context, timeout or budget, card not fit (R8 reason codes)
A harness edit names the component it changes and predicts its effect on a named measure over a stated volume of work
The edit runs as a trial configuration on the same work (R20) and is adopted through the Release Gate only if its prediction held (X17); otherwise it is reverted
A harness that serves unlike work badly branches by tier or domain rather than accumulating special cases

Promotion (R25): a stable, repeated pattern of agent work is proposed as a deterministic path (workflow, view or engine function), run alongside the agents on the same requests, and adopted if it matches at lower cost; its rejects return as exception cards
acceptance: Every adopted harness edit has a recorded prediction and its measured outcome
A failed prediction reverts the edit automatically
A model swap is never recorded as a harness improvement
evidence: Harness change log with predictions and outcomes

cards.title: Audit marks the tests: mutation score
cards.intent: A test suite that cannot fail proves nothing. Audit measures whether sealed and challenge tests catch planted mutations.
scope: Mutation score of each sampled card's sealed and challenge tests: the share of planted code mutations they catch
A suite below the standard is handed back to its author (R21, R8): Planning for sealed tests, the challenge tester for its own
Standard per tier [PROPOSED]: reported only until Isa sets it with AR-08's other standards
Planted defects (C2.01) include defects inside failure scenarios, so sealed tests are marked too
acceptance: Every audited card carries a mutation score
A suite below the standard is handed back with its score

cards.title: Voice front end: live speech, English and Arabic
cards.intent: Speak to the Factory and get answers back as you talk. Live speech-to-text streams through the gateway to any model on the menu, for Isa and, later, EvryMynd users.
scope: Mobile microphone to streaming speech-to-text to the gateway (C0.19) to the chosen model; a reply by voice where the user asks for one
English and Arabic from the first release; accuracy measured per language and dialect (Gulf and Moroccan Arabic separately), and the provider chosen on measured accuracy, latency and cost, not claims
Rolling transcript windows: send only what changed; cheap models for routine notes, frontier models on request (R14 prices them)
Once the Council runs (C3.02), a spoken question can go to the council and come back with its sources

Prototype first (Isa, 5 Oct 2026): Isa is the only user, on her own provider accounts; consent, vendor terms, processing location for sovereign users and anything touching health data wait for the pre-release gate (OI-21)
acceptance: Word error rate, latency and cost per hour are reported per language and dialect

cards.title: Inquiry
cards.intent: Independent discovery: commit before seeing any other submission.
scope: Participants on the same brief, committing before any peer output is visible
Sizing: the institutional model found two analysts sufficient (Idea Record §5.3); X7 tests universal participation. Live data decides (C4.01)
Harness (Inquiry, framing): repository read and Ledger retrieval, no write; sees the brief and engineering context only
acceptance: No participant sees a peer output or identity before committing
evidence: Manifest audit of what each participant saw

cards.title: Deliberation Council
cards.intent: Shared understanding without prestige or dominance.
scope: Anonymous labels; random reading order; no chair; no vote
Every proposition appears in the synthesis; one objection keeps a point disputed
One round (Idea Record §5.3)
Output: the Alignment Record for Isa's ratification, with minority positions
Harness (Council, framing): anonymised submissions and a synthesis writer only
acceptance: No identity is visible to Council participants
Every Inquiry proposition is traceable in the synthesis

cards.title: Planning Chamber
cards.intent: Intent to executable cards: blind parallel decomposition, then reconciliation and a separate red team. Until it exists, cards come from this pack and from splits and returns under R8.
scope: Decomposers blind in parallel; reconciler; red team separate from the reconciler
One planner plus a red team (Idea Record §5.3)
Plans name the interfaces between requirements (DQ11)
Tier-setting rules (C1.02)
Harness (Planning, planning): repository read and a schema-checked card writer; sees the Alignment Record with minority positions, never the Council transcript
acceptance: Planning sees the Alignment Record, including minority positions, never the Council transcript
Every card traces to a requirement in the Alignment Record

cards.title: Ratification tiers and Isa's attention budget
cards.intent: Human ratification is the likely real ceiling. Route to Isa only what the rules say needs her.
scope: Which ideas need Isa's ratification and which the Council may ratify (AR-09b)
Isa's attention is measured, not budgeted, because her time varies (Isa, 1 Oct 2026); alerts when an idea outside the envelope waits more than a week
Isa's fixed touchpoints: standards, Alignment Records, amendments, governance changes at the Release Gate, R13 escalations
The envelope and attention queue run from Phase 1 (C1.22); once the Council exists, its Alignment Records are what the envelope ratifies
acceptance: Every ratification request cites the rule that routed it to Isa
Weekly attention hours are reported (M17)

cards.title: Typed propositions: failure scenarios and opportunities
cards.intent: Ideation feeds testing. Inquiry participants commit typed propositions, including the edge cases they would test, so blind spots that differ by family surface before any code exists.
scope: Proposition types: interpretation, requirement, assumption, risk, objection, alternative, opportunity, failure scenario
Every participant names failure scenarios blind, before seeing peers (commit before view)
Failure scenarios the Council keeps enter the Alignment Record's acceptance criteria and become sealed tests (C1.20)
Originated briefs (C1.21) are pulled by Inquiry like Isa's; their opportunities are judged later by realised value (X22)
Surviving propositions per model are recorded by type (X7)
acceptance: Every proposition has a type and cites its evidence
Every failure scenario the Council keeps traces to a sealed test in at least one card

cards.title: Dissent credited by outcome
cards.intent: Mark the Council on what happened, not only on what was approved. Overruled dissent that proved right earns credit; assumptions are marked held or failed.
scope: At ratification, record the open assumptions and which minority positions were accepted or overruled (R32)
When outcomes arrive (realised value from C0.09, incidents, change failures), link them back to the Alignment Record
Credit the Inquiry contributions behind overruled positions the outcome supports; mark each assumption held, failed or unclear
Unclear outcomes stay unclear; nothing is forced
Lessons (C1.24) may be proposed from failed assumptions
acceptance: Every ratified Alignment Record lists its open assumptions and overruled positions
Every recorded outcome is linked to its Alignment Record with a held, failed or unclear mark per assumption

cards.title: The Council against a single-model baseline
cards.intent: The Council must earn its cost. Compare Inquiry plus the Council with one strong model framing alone on the same briefs, and drop deliberation steps that do not pay.
scope: On a sample of briefs, one strong model also drafts the Alignment Record alone, blind to the Council's draft
Compare material omissions found later, Isa's send-backs, her review time and cost per clean idea (X24)
A deliberation step that does not pay is proposed for removal through the Release Gate and Isa
The result also tests EvryMynd's agent council offer
acceptance: The comparison is reported with sample size, and judged against X24's criterion when the sample suffices

cards.title: Judge X1-X14 continuously
cards.intent: Each experiment can prove the idea wrong. Judge each as live data accrues, and turn a falsified one into an amendment card.
scope: Each experiment X1-X14 judged against its falsification criterion in the pack, on live data, whenever it has enough
A falsified experiment opens an amendment card to the Release Gate and Isa (principle 8)
When every institution is running, retire the old role routing's code through the Release Gate; keep its history in the Ledger
acceptance: Every experiment carries a current verdict (not falsified / falsified / not enough data yet, with the data used)
